description: One-pass review of crate jmap-base-client (crate-jmap-base-client/). Filed by /review-rusty-crate. NOTE: This is a LOCKED crate per AGENTS.md — findings will be filed but cannot be acted on without explicit user approval per change.
notes:
Maintainer risk: LOW — small surface, well-isolated module boundaries, exhaustive ClientError match in tests, all I/O caps configurable; main risk is the third-party error leakage in Http/WebSocket variants which fossilizes a reqwest/tungstenite major-version dependency on every downstream caller.
Correctness confidence: 92% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: extract_response with multiple-invocation-per-call_id (JMAP-6lsm.1) — needs spec/RFC re-read to confirm whether servers actually emit duplicate call_ids in practice; SSE Content-Type subtype-prefix matching (JMAP-6lsm.2) — low impact but real semantics gap. Uncertainty driven by: (1) WS error handling under partial-frame conditions (only tested via successful happy paths); (2) integration with extension crates jmap-mail-client/jmap-chat-client not in scope here; (3) live-server behavior under network reset/timeout differs from wiremock.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — passes default clippy cleanly. Pedantic surfaces real items (parse_ws_frame unconditional clone in hot path JMAP-6lsm.11; URL-scheme stringy allocations JMAP-6lsm.9, JMAP-6lsm.10; trait-object blanket-impl maintenance JMAP-6lsm.19) and several opinion-tagged style nits. Overall the code reads as written by a careful Rust author who knows the borrow checker; the issues that are real are design decisions that have hardened, not idiom violations.
Rust idiom confidence: 88% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: AuthProvider trait-object lifetime ergonomics for async credential schemes (JMAP-6lsm.20) — may have a simpler workaround I haven't seen; ClientError::Parse context-loss (JMAP-6lsm.21) — there might be an idiomatic context-injection pattern that doesn't require enum reshape. Uncertainty driven by: (1) no exposure to the full caller surface in jmap-mail-client / jmap-chat-client to see how trait objects are actually used downstream; (2) didn't run cargo doc to inspect rendered intra-doc links.
LOCKED CRATE NOTE: this crate's AGENTS.md prohibits any code change without explicit per-change user approval. All findings filed under this epic are review-only. Working through them requires a separate non-headless session where the user can approve each change individually. Several findings (e.g. JMAP-6lsm.4 max_upload_body rename, JMAP-6lsm.22 third-party error leakage) are public-API-affecting and may not be approved at all.
title: Review: jmap-base-client rusty pass
